profile.address: Calle de Alfonso Gómez 4, Madrid, 28037, Spain
profile.reading:
MAD4 is a Digital Realty colocation building at Calle de Alfonso Gómez 4, in the Julian Camarillo and Barajas data center corridor on the eastern side of Madrid, Spain. Digital Realty's own Madrid metro page lists MAD4 alongside three other individually numbered buildings it operates in the same metro area, MAD1 on Calle Albasanz 71, MAD2 on Calle Albasanz 73, and MAD3 on Calle Emilio Muñoz 49, each on a different street rather than clustered on one shared physical campus. That MAD1 through MAD4 numbering belongs to Digital Realty alone and happens to echo, without being related to, the separate MAD01 and MAD02 campus codes that DATA4, an unrelated French headquartered operator also tracked in this registry, uses for its own Madrid facilities nearby. Readers comparing both operators' Madrid footprints should not conflate the two numbering systems.

Digital Realty's own property page for this building lists 228,000 square feet, about 21,200 square meters, of colocation space, with 2N UPS power redundancy and N+1 cooling redundancy. The page lists LEED Gold certification with a claim of 100 percent renewable energy sourcing, plus a certification roster covering ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 20000-1, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, Spain's ENS national security scheme for systems serving public administration, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS. Physical security includes onsite personnel, biometric and photo badge access control, and CCTV footage retained for 30 days. Digital Realty markets the space as scalable from multi megawatt suites down to single cabinet colocation deployments under its PlatformDIGITAL brand.

Neither Digital Realty's MAD4 property page nor its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission publishes a megawatt figure, critical IT load, standby generator rating, or onsite generation figure for this specific building. Digital Realty Trust, SEC filer CIK 1297996, headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street in Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, split between 221 wholly owned or consolidated properties and 89 held in unconsolidated joint ventures, spanning about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets. Its FY2025 10-K discloses this international portfolio, including Spain, at the region and country level rather than building by building, a pattern this registry has found consistent across every Digital Realty property researched. Digital Realty operates as a colocation and wholesale data center landlord serving enterprise and cloud tenants, distinct from a hyperscaler that runs its own compute.

One third party facility directory lists a 5 megawatt figure for this property. That figure does not appear on any Digital Realty page or SEC filing reviewed this session, so it is not adopted here as fact, and no IT capacity, utility power, standby generation, or onsite generation figure is recorded for MAD4 in this registry. No tenant name, opening year, or floor count for this specific building was found in operator or regulatory sources. Madrid's Julian Camarillo and Barajas district functions as one of the city's established interconnection hubs, and Naturgy and Iberdrola remain the principal Spanish utilities serving commercial and industrial power demand, including data centers, across the Madrid metro area.
